paper.title: Warm-starting Contextual Bandits: Robustly Combining Supervised and Bandit Feedback

unmapped: Learner additionally receives n_s fully supervised warm-start examples from a different distribution D^s with the same context marginal; D^s is (alpha, Delta)-similar to the CB distribution D^b (unknown to learner)
Regret is measured against best policy in a finite policy class Pi via conditional expected costs given realized contexts
settings.definition_quote: The learner receives $\Ss$, a dataset of $\ns$ fully supervised examples drawn i.i.d. from $\Ds$. ... For $t = 1,2,\ldots,\nb$, the environment draws $(x_t, \cb_t) \sim \Db$ and reveals $x_t$ to the learner, based on which the learner chooses a (possibly random) action $a_t \in [K]$ and observes $\cb_t(a_t)$... In the CB ground truth setting ... the goal of the learner is to optimize the costs drawn from distribution $\Db$

unmapped: Regret is measured on supervised cost distribution D^s, while bandit feedback during interaction comes from a different distribution D^b that is (alpha, Delta)-similar to D^s
Learner receives n_s supervised warm-start examples from D^s
settings.definition_quote: In the CB ground truth setting (resp. supervised ground truth setting), the goal of the learner is to optimize the costs drawn from distribution $\Db$ (resp. $\Ds$).

settings.name_in_paper: 2-armed bandit with biased warm start (failure of simple strategies)
unmapped: Learner receives n_s warm-start examples with deterministic costs (0.5, 0.5+Delta/2) while bandit costs are (0.5, 0.5-Delta/2)
settings.definition_quote: this is a $2$-armed bandit setting (i.e. contextual bandits with a dummy context)... $\cs_0 = (0.5, 0.5 + \frac \Delta 2), \quad \mbox{and} \quad \cb_0 = (0.5, 0.5 - \frac \Delta 2)$.

settings.name_in_paper: Combining two sources in supervised learning
settings.out_of_scope_reason: Offline supervised learning (binary classification) from two sources; no interaction.

symbols.N_exp: size of the finite policy class |Pi|
symbols.G_min: min over lambda in Lambda of sum_{t=1}^{T} G_t(lambda, alpha, Delta), with G_t = ((1-lambda) n_s Delta + 2 V_t(lambda)) / (lambda t + (1-lambda) n_s alpha), V_t(lambda) = 2 sqrt((lambda^2 K t/eps + (1-lambda)^2 n_s) ln(8 T |Pi|/delta)) + (lambda K/eps + (1-lambda)) ln(8 T |Pi|/delta)

conditions: D^s is (alpha, Delta)-similar to D^b w.r.t. Pi

source.label: thm:bandit-gt

results.notes: Paper bounds average regret; multiplied by T. Regret defined via conditional expected costs given contexts. The min-over-lambda term encoded as declared symbol G_min.

source.label: cor:bandit-gt-01

results.notes: Average regret multiplied by T. The epsilon term is outside the O in the paper. Paper notes eps = T^{-2/3} gives O(T^{2/3}) regret.

symbols.n_epochs: number of epochs E = ceil(log T)
symbols.H_min: min over lambda in Lambda of (2/T) sum_{t=1}^T (lambda Delta + 2 W_t(lambda))/((1-lambda) + lambda alpha), W_t(lambda) = 2 sqrt((lambda^2 K/(t eps) + (1-lambda)^2 (E+1)/n_s) ln(8E|Pi|/delta)) + (lambda K/(t eps) + (1-lambda)(E+1)/n_s) ln(8E|Pi|/delta)

conditions: D^b is (alpha, Delta)-similar to D^s w.r.t. Pi
